walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 2: Comparative Essay — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 2: Comparative Essay brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 2: Comparative Essay.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term unreliable narrator in 1961?
options: Wayne Booth
Northrop Frye
F R Leavis
Mikhail Bakhtin

mcqs.q: Which Marquez novel exemplifies magic realism?
options: Love in the Time of Cholera
One Hundred Years of Solitude
The Autumn of the Patriarch
Chronicle of a Death Foretold
Subtle hints or clues earlier in a text that anticipate later events, making the resolution feel both surprising and inevitable.
Foreshadowing is when a character predicts the future.
A theme is the title of the book.
Foreshadowing is the shadow a character casts in a scene.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a theme and a symbol?
options: A theme is the title of the book.
Themes are just symbols repeated through the book.
A theme is an abstract idea or concern the text explores (e.g. mortality); a symbol is a concrete image that stands for something else (e.g. a skull).
Verbal irony is when you make a joke about something.
Verbal irony is just saying something unexpected.
A theme is the title of the book.
Verbal irony is when you make a joke about something.
When a speaker says one thing but means another — typically the opposite — relying on shared context for the listener to detect the gap.
